comparator.sourceNotes: The official prospective year pages sum to 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of 60 EC compulsory sociology, social problems, survey research, statistics, policy and professional development; zero-credit RADAr is omitted. Year two has 42 EC compulsory theory, lifestyle, statistics, regression, measurement, social research and professional development; 12 EC restricted sociology electives chosen as the first two 6-EC items in published order; and 6 EC genuinely free choice. The alternative Diversities in Care comprises two inseparable 5+1 EC units, and is not counted on this route. Year three has 26 EC compulsory theory/methods/professional development, 12 EC free choice, a compulsory 13-EC labour-market internship and a 9-EC bachelor thesis. The 18 EC free choice across years two and three is left open. These pages are indicative and do not guarantee individual course availability in a future entrant cohort.

alternatives.label: Sociology, inequality and social research
alternatives.concept: Studies sociological theory, social groups, conflict and inequality alongside survey design, quantitative and qualitative methods. Law, economics, media and psychology illuminate social problems without replacing the sociology core; the Radboud internship and independent thesis remain distinct requirements.
alternatives.labelReason: Four dedicated UCR sociology courses are reinforced by political, legal, psychological and statistical study of inequality and group relations; the label accurately signals an interdisciplinary sociology response.
progression: Introductory sociology, politics and research precede advanced social theory, statistics, policy and media; formal prerequisites and term offerings are satisfied.

alternatives.label: Social inequality and political change
alternatives.concept: Asks how social divisions, migration, public debate and political institutions shape inequality and collective responses, including environmental justice and policy. It retains the sociology and research foundation while shifting advanced work toward politics, law, media and sustainability governance.
alternatives.labelReason: The course schedule contains sociology, comparative and EU politics, criminal law, media, climate and governance, supporting an explicit policy and political-change emphasis.
progression: The introductory sociology, politics and law courses precede upper-level theory, policy-related law and sustainability governance; all formal prerequisites and term offerings are satisfied.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces psychology, experimental methods, developmental psychology and econometric emphasis with political philosophy, historical context, rights, climate communication and sustainability governance; the questions shift from measuring social experience toward explaining political responses and institutions.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary bachelor with first two listed 6-EC sociology electives in year two
routeSelection.basis: The generic Sociology target has no named specialization. In the year-two choose-two-of-three set, Political Change and Opposition and Climate change & inequality are the first two listed 6-EC units; the 6-EC Diversities in Care combination is the unselected third choice. This selection follows source order independently of UCR fit. The 18 EC of free space remains genuinely open.

selection.assessment: Two coherent, independently evidenced UCR schedules are feasible and differ in social-science emphasis and at least four courses. A third distinct programme would require an unsupported standalone specialization in demography, migration, family studies or sociology fieldwork; repackaging adjacent psychology or law modules would duplicate the two supported directions.

notes.text: Radboud has a continuous disciplinary sociology sequence, successive supervised survey/research projects, a required labour-market internship and a sociology thesis. UCR can build a strong interdisciplinary social-science response but its sociology course set is smaller and the credited project, internship and thesis requirements are not treated as equivalent to ordinary courses.
